text:
hana: Posting Pegasus postmortem follow-ups. Root cause summary: customer on-prem load balancer rewrote source ports + route-map normalization mismatch, which broke our affinity tokens and produced connection tombstones in the dedicated runtime, causing a partial tenant isolation cascade. I pulled the remediation items and tentative owners.
mike: Can you list compact owners/timeline so we can triage into the sprint?
hana: Short list: (1) infra: route-map normalization + peering filter update, (2) runtime: affinity token validation + soft-evict, (3) DevEx: harness to simulate port-rewrite + token loss, (4) customer coord + comms, (5) monthly pattern scan for affinity-related incidents.

kevin-runtime: I'll own runtime changes (PEG-6001). Plan: on detection of affinity token mismatch mark connections as "suspect" and perform a staggered soft-evict with sticky recon attempts rather than immediate hard eviction. Also add explicit token-validation metrics. Prototype this week.
devex: I'll build a harness (PEG-6002) that simulates source-port rewrite and route-map normalization differences so we can reproduce token mismatch and validate the soft-evict behavior. Will wire into nightly regression after demo.

mike: Infra will own peering/config work (PEG-6003). Tasks: add route-map normalization rules to prefer canonical source-port mapping, add a small TCP probe which validates that our affinity token roundtrip survives for 30s, and add a canary allowlist. PR target: Thu EOD.

infra-bot: created tickets PEG-6001, PEG-6002, PEG-6003 by hana.

hana: Customer comms (PEG-6004): I'll draft a short runbook for Pegasus network team recommending they avoid aggressive source-port rewrite for peered flows and to validate route-map symmetry; propose maintenance slot Mon 23:00 UTC for them to test.

kevin-runtime: Proposed runtime checklist items (to add to PEG-6001):
- detect affinity_token.mismatch across 5s -> mark_connection_suspect
- perform soft_eviction window 8-20s with per-tenant jitter to avoid herd effects
- trigger token_probe: active validate token roundtrip then restore sticky state
- emit metrics: affinity.token_mismatch_count, conn.suspect_count, conn.soft_evictions

kevin-runtime: quick pseudo-snippet:
```
def on_token_mismatch(conn):
    conn.mark_suspect(ttl=20)
    schedule(conn.attempt_sticky_reconnect, delay=rand(3,9))
    if conn.sticky_reconnects > 3:
        conn.hard_evict()
```

devex: Harness tests: (A) port rewrite causing token mismatch -> assert no tenant-wide hard-eviction under soft-evict logic; (B) intermittent token loss with reconverge -> assert max 1 eviction per 50k requests. Will add a failing test initially to demonstrate regression.

mike: Infra snippet for reviewers (gated during canary):
```bash
# Normalize route-map to preserve source-port semantics for peered prefixes
# example pseudo-config
route-map RM-PEER normalize permit 10
 set ip source-port preserve
exit
# fallback: allow established, then drop unexpected
iptables -A INPUT -s <peer-cidr> -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s <peer-cidr> -j DROP
```

mike: Note: DROP will be enabled behind a canary allowlist and only after 30m stable metrics.

hana: Success criteria to attach to tickets:
- synthetic port-rewrite test shows zero tenant isolation for 10m after changes
- soft-eviction reduces hard-evictions by >=90% in canary window
- affinity.token_mismatch_count falls to <1% of prior baseline in canary
- customer confirms test of route-map normalization within 3 business days

sre-oncall: I'll monitor canary and standby for rollback. Add a Kibana saved query to PRs: kql: message:eviction AND tenant:pegasus AND timestamp:[now-30m TO now].

devex: Proposed schedule:
- PEG-6002 harness -> prototype Wed, demo Thu AM
- PEG-6001 runtime -> prototype Thu, PR Mon
- PEG-6003 infra -> PR Thu EOD, canary Sat 00:30-01:30 UTC (30% peered prefixes)
- PEG-6004 comms -> hana to send Mon EOD

hana: I'll create sprint cards and a 30m handoff invite for Thu 09:30 PT. If owners need to reassign or change windows, reply in-thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
